## Reading the variable-name mapping and value labels


```{r , include = FALSE}
download_root  <- "~/Desktop/Masterarbeit/Data/download/Exp1_Feb+June23"
values_root    <- "~/Desktop/Masterarbeit/Data"
project_root <- "~/Desktop/GitHub/DoesMediaQualityMatter"
output_dir <- file.path(project_root, "Output", "00_setup")
```


```{r , include = TRUE}
#output_dir <- file.path(project_root, "Output", "00_setup")
#project_root <- ""

wave_files <- tibble::tribble(
  ~wave,  ~varnames_path,                                                        ~varvalues_path,
  "T0",   file.path(download_root, "T0_Feb23_base",   "T0_Feb_varnames.xlsx"),   file.path(values_root, "Variablenwerte.xlsx"),
  "T1",   file.path(download_root, "T1-3_June23_exp", "T1_June_varnames.xlsx"),  file.path(values_root, "Variablenwerte_T1.xlsx"),
  "T2",   file.path(download_root, "T1-3_June23_exp", "T2_June_varnames.xlsx"),  file.path(values_root, "Variablenwerte_T2.xlsx"),
  "T3",   file.path(download_root, "T1-3_June23_exp", "T3_June_varnames.xlsx"),  file.path(values_root, "Variablenwerte_T3.xlsx")
)
```

```{r lookup-read}
save_both <- function(obj, name, dir = output_dir) {
  saveRDS(obj, file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".Rds")))
  write.csv(obj, file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  message("Saved ", name)
}

# The value-label files carry a varying number of title rows before the real
# data starts (T0: 1, T1: 1, T2/T3: 2), and the June files head their columns
# "Wert"/"Label" rather than leaving them blank. So instead of a fixed [-1, ],
# read with no header, find the row where the data block begins, and take the
# first three columns as id / value / label. The variable-ID column is only
# filled on each block's first row, so fill() carries it down.
read_value_labels <- function(path) {
  raw <- read_excel(path, sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE, .name_repair = "minimal")

  # Data begins on the row *after* the "Wert" header (June files); for the
  # Feb file there is no "Wert" row, so fall back to dropping the single
  # title row, matching the original T0 behaviour.
  wert_row <- which(raw[[1]] == "Wert")
  first_data_row <- if (length(wert_row) > 0) wert_row[1] + 1 else 2

  raw[first_data_row:nrow(raw), 1:3] %>%
    rlang::set_names(c("variable_id", "value_code", "label_text")) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
    fill(variable_id) %>%
    filter(!is.na(variable_id) | !is.na(value_code) | !is.na(label_text))
}

lookups <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(wave_files))) {
  wave <- wave_files$wave[i]

  var_values <- read_value_labels(wave_files$varvalues_path[i])

  var_mapping <- read_excel(wave_files$varnames_path[i]) %>%
    # Column name for the variable name differs per wave: T0 Var_Name,
    # T1-2 Varname, T3 Varnames. Harmonize to Var_Name.
    rename(Var_Name = any_of(c("Varname", "Varnames"))) %>%
    mutate(Variable = as.character(Variable), Var_Name = as.character(Var_Name))

  lookup <- var_values %>%
    left_join(var_mapping %>% select(Variable, Var_Name, Label),
              by = c("variable_id" = "Variable"))

  # Guard: if almost nothing matched, the ID systems don't line up -- fail
  # loudly rather than silently saving an all-NA sheet.
  matched <- sum(!is.na(lookup$Var_Name))
  message(wave, ": ", matched, " of ", nrow(lookup), " value rows matched a variable name.")
  if (matched == 0) warning(wave, ": no keys matched between value labels and varnames -- check the ID columns.")

  save_both(lookup, paste0("clean_variable_lookup_sheet_", wave))
  lookups[[wave]] <- lookup
}
```
